04 / CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS

Good Buildings Begin Below the Surface.

A building's character is visible in its roofline and siding. Its lasting value begins with the decisions beneath them: the site, foundation, framing and materials.

FROM THE GROUND UP

Illustrative floor assembly · Diagram not to scale

01 / THE FOUNDATION

Start with the Site.

For a typical 10′ × 12′ building, our reference pad measures 14′ × 16′—allowing two feet of preparation beyond the structure on every side. The approach begins with subgrade preparation, geotextile separation, a compacted stone base and appropriate moisture management.

Pressure-treated structural beams support a framed floor above the prepared base. The final foundation arrangement is planned around the building and conditions at your property.

Explore Our Construction Approach ↗
02 / FLOOR

Solid Underfoot.

Our standard floor assembly specifies 6×6 pressure-treated support beams, 2×6 pressure-treated joists at 16 inches on center and ¾-inch pressure-treated plywood. Larger buildings may require different framing.

03 / EXTERIOR

Materials You Can Choose.

Exterior choices include vinyl, DuraTemp, LP board-and-batten, cedar lap and cedar shake. Available options vary by model and are identified on the individual pricing pages.

04 / CONSTRUCTION

Built on Your Property.

Our buildings are constructed on-site. We review access, preparation requirements and the building's specifications before establishing the written project scope.

05 / COMMITMENT

Warranty in Writing.

Appalachian Sheds offers a 30-year structural warranty. The written warranty defines its coverage, limitations and maintenance requirements.

Know the structure behind the style.

View Construction Details ↗

05 / DESIGN & INSPIRATION

Architecture That Belongs.
Space That Works.

A backyard building should feel at home on the property and serve a real purpose. Appalachian rooflines, considered proportions and natural materials create the starting point. How you use the space is up to you.

APPALACHIAN FORMS · ARCHITECTURAL STUDY

Architectural illustration · Not a photograph of a completed building

THE IDEA BEHIND THE DESIGN

Rooted in the Mountains.
Designed for Today's Backyard.

Steep gables, saltbox slopes, lean-to forms and generous overhangs come from a practical building tradition. We take their character seriously, then consider the shape, scale and function that best suit your property.
